Accidental Release Prevention and Emergency Response Policies:
Amrize is dedicated to protecting employees, the community, and the environment from
highly hazardous incidents through safely operating our facility.
Accidental Release Prevention and Emergency Response Policies:
The Charleston facility's overall approach and commitment to chemical safety is
demonstrated by 1) the management, training, procedure, and maintenance systems in
place at the facility, and 2) the hazard assessment, prevention program and emergency
response provisions implemented specifically for the covered flammables in response to
the RMP requirement. The management structure and oversight to ensure safety is
documented in the facility's RMP and includes compliance with applicable regulations,
codes and standards (OSHA PSM Standard and US EPA 40 CFR PART 68).
Source and Federal Regulated Substances Description:
The Charleston facility uses a chemical blend, containing n-pentane and isopentane, as
the blowing agent to manufacture foam panels for use in the building industry. The
blend consists of varying amounts of n-pentane and isopentane and is reported as a
flammable mixture. The covered process includes raw material unloading and storage,
material blending operations, panel production and cutting, finished product storage and
shipping operations.
General Accidental Release Prevention Program and Chemical-Specific
Prevention Steps:
The facility has implemented a Program Level 3 Program for the covered process, as
required by the RMP rule, in accordance with the US EPA guidance. The covered
chemicals are also regulated under OSHAs Process Safety Management (PSM)
regulation. Therefore, the Charleston facility has a comprehensive PSM/RMP
Prevention Program. These prevention program provisions are specifically intended to
minimize the probability and/or consequence of any accidental release from the facility
and include such measures as process hazards analysis, operating procedures,
training

, contractors, pre-start-up safety, mechanical integrity, hot work permit,
management of change, incident investigation, emergency planning and response, and
compliance audits. The facility prevention program is an ongoing system based on
periodic training, incident investigations, audits, procedure revisions, and RMP updates
as required to reflect facility change and RMP requirements.
Five-year Accident History:
The facility has had no RMP reportable accidents or releases of the covered chemicals.
 Emergency Response Program:
The facilitys Emergency Action Plan is intended to produce the maximum response in
the least amount of time. The Charleston facility is considered a defensive responder
and will rely on outside responders and resources in the event of an emergency. The
facility has established notification mechanisms as well as ongoing coordination
activities with the Charleston Fire Department to ensure timely communication and a
safe response to any accidental release from the facility.
 Planned changes to improve safety:
The facility is committed to ensuring its operations are safe and in accordance with all
RMP requirements and has established a senior manager responsible for RMP
development, implementation, and compliance. This manager is committed to maintain
the safety of the RMP covered process through active adherence to the appropriate
procedures and codes. To ensure that the appropriate changes occur as necessary to
maintain/improve safety, ongoing hazard reviews, training, audits, maintenance, and
investigations will be conducted as required by RMP. Updates to the RMP will be
completed as necessary in response to these activities.
Amrize takes pride in and is committed to conducting business in strict conformity with
all applicable laws in a safe and responsible manner. The very highest priority is placed
on the health and safety of Amrize's teammates and the community in which we
conduct business.
